title: observability-token-kv-cost-latency-dashboard-alert-tuning-extend-metrics-tracing
author: Diego Ramos
release_notes: Add token-level KV cache cost + latency dashboard, extend tracing spans to include model/variant/route labels, and tune alert thresholds to reduce noisy incidents. Rolling rollout with canary followed by full deployment.
description:
Motivation: We need better observability of token-level costs and latency for requests that hit/miss the KV cache and across model variants/routes to diagnose regressions and optimize serving economics. Current dashboards surface aggregate token cost and p95 latency but lack per-route/variant/kv-hit breakdowns and tracing linkages, making investigations slow and noisy. This PR adds token-level KV cache metrics, expands tracing spans, introduces a Grafana dashboard with cost/latency breakdowns by route/model/variant and tunes alerting to reduce false positives while preserving SLO coverage.

What this PR does:
- Instrument serving runtime to emit kv_cache.hit_count, kv_cache.miss_count, kv_cache.size_bytes (per-model, per-variant, per-route labels).
- Add token-level metrics: tokens.generated_total, tokens.requested_total with label dimensions (route, model, variant, kv_hit).
- Add cost-per-token time series (derived metric) and per-1M-token cost summaries for dashboards.
- Extend OpenTelemetry tracing spans to annotate span attributes: model.name, model.variant, route.id, kv.cache_hit (boolean), batch.size.
- Update Grafana: new dashboard "Token-level KV cost & latency" with panels for p50/p90/p95 token latency by KV-hit, cost breakdown by model/variant/route, and heatmap of batch sizes vs latency.
- Alert tuning: consolidate noisy alerts into grouped alerts with improved thresholds and longer evaluation windows: p95_token_latency_high (route/model-scoped), cost_regression_detected (relative increase >20% over 7d baseline), kv_miss_ratio_high (when kv_miss_ratio > 5% for 30m).
- Add runbook entries and escalation steps for the above alerts, wired into the SRE on-call rotation.
- Feature flagging and rollout: metrics emit guarded behind feature flag obs.token_kv_v2; rollout plan is 10% canary -> 50% -> 100% via service-config rollout.
- Tests: unit tests for new metrics emission, integration test that validates OpenTelemetry span attributes and basic dashboard panels using test data.

Files of interest (high-level):
- serving/runtime/kv_metrics.go: new metric exporters and label construction hooks.
- serving/runtime/kv_metrics_test.go: unit tests for metrics labels and cardinality controls.
- serving/tracing/trace_attributes.go: add new span attributes for model/variant/route/kv_hit.
- observability/grafana/token_kv_cost_dashboard.json: dashboard JSON, panels and variables.
- observability/alerts/token_kv_alerts.yaml: Prometheus alert rules and descriptions.
- docs/observability/token_kv_dashboard.md: user-facing docs and runbooks.
- ci/integration/obs_integration_test.py: integration harness that spins up local observability stack and validates emitted metrics/spans.

Commits:
- 7a3b2f4  add: kv cache token-level metrics and cardinality controls
- b2d9c11  feat: extend tracing spans with model/variant/route attributes
- c4f1e2a  docs: dashboard guide + runbooks
- d9f6a77  ci: add integration test for token-level metrics/tracing

Testing and validation:
- Local integration runs with Jaeger + Prometheus + Grafana passed on canary service config.
- Unit tests added; CI passed all checks after addressing test flakiness (see CI checks).
- Canary rollout (internal) for 10% of production traffic for 48h showed stable metric cardinality and no alert noise increase.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main behind feature flag obs.token_kv_v2 disabled by default.
2) Enable for 10% via service-config for 48h, monitor new dashboard and cardinality metrics.
3) If stable, ramp to 50% then 100% over 72h windows, with ability to rollback via service-config.

Notes/Limitations:
- To avoid cardinality explosion labels are limited to model.family (not full model hash) and route.id is bucketed to top-100 routes; longer tail routes labeled "other". See cardinality controls in kv_metrics.go.
- Cost-per-token is estimated using current pricing config; absolute cost numbers are for relative comparison and will be surfaced as estimated.

References: ENG-1987, ENG-2021, SUP-412.

review_comments: Anya Patel: This is great progress — my only concern is cardinality. Can we confirm the top-100 route bucketing won't hide important regressions for small but high-priority routes?

Diego Ramos: Answered — we added an optional label route.priority that remains low-cardinality (high/normal/low) and we surface 'top-100' vs 'other' as a dashboard filter. Added tests to validate bucket assignment.
Sofia Martin: Please add a smoke check that validates span attributes are present in OpenTelemetry exports. Without spans we lose context during incidents.
Diego Ramos: Added integration smoke test (ci/integration/obs_integration_test.py) to assert presence of model.name, model.variant, route.id and kv.cache_hit attributes in spans. CI green after fix.
Michael Chen: Alert thresholds look reasonable but can still be chatty on small routes. Suggest grouping alerts by route and using a suppression window for low-traffic routes.
Diego Ramos: Implemented grouped alerts with a min_samples=50 (PromQL) and longer evaluation window for low-traffic routes. Updated runbook accordingly.
